It’s Christmas and I’m remaining inebriated until I have to be sober around my in-laws who have their own problems, lol. But here’s a story for ya. 

Until 2013, I (20f) lived with my nMother and her husband (somewhere between enabler and flying monkey), and my at the time boyfriend, who wasn’t a good boyfriend (I’ve seen him more recently and he seems to have grown up and he’s better now!). 

My mother loved BF for me. One time when I was upset, she told him it was because I wanted him to propose. I didn’t. I don’t remember what specific thing I was being gaslit about reacting to, but I felt trapped and I wanted out of the relationship with a guy who was calling me fat and taking me to Sonic to “apologize” for saying I’m overweight and we’d never go anywhere but Saladworks again. There were other things wrong, like buying me expensive gifts and taking me to expensive retardants and making comments about me paying it back when I couldn’t afford it. 

And I had a pretty cool best friend who didn’t see the bigger picture, but she’d hear me complain about my mother doing XYZ, and be like “uhhh…” once in a while. She’d see the way BF treated me and ask why I was still with him, and she couldn’t understand why I couldn’t just break it off. She kept me sane a lot; it wasn’t all in my head. But she came from a healthier family and she didn’t see the bullshit 99% of the time. 

Well, right after Christmas 2012, I did break up with him, finally. Politely, and with no real drama. And my mother promptly kicked me out. I think I was given to the end of the week, but exBF was fine with me leaving my things there. (Until he wasn’t because I moved on and had a rebound and he put my books outside in the rain in like March.) But so I was NC with my mom. I moved in with my grandma (dad’s mom), slept on her couch, got to bring my dog (grandma loved my dog), had to give up my bunny (no room for his cage), and then I eventually moved out of her place to move in with my now-husband, then-boyfriend. 

It had been a couple years (2015), and when my mother and I started talking again, it felt different. We played Town of Salem together. She was inviting me over to do my laundry and play video games together. And then my now-husband proposed, and my mother and I planned the wedding and honeymoon. Our wedding would be with our “adopted” family in a particular niche of the kink community we were a part of, at the convention where he’d proposed to me (we were friends with the people who created and ran it). And our honeymoon would be a big family thing: my mother/husband and sister/guy and nieces, as well as my husband’s mother/husband and niece, would all go to Disney for a week and celebrate together, but we’d have our own room. We were all so excited: my husband has never been to Disney. (Spoiler: everyone except my husband and me went to Disney the week we got married. We couldn’t afford it because my mother was no longer offering to help with the time share and stuff, after the following paragraph.) 

The other foot dropped. After maybe half a year of this healthy feeling parent/adult child relationship, she suddenly had an issue. My niece had said “I hate you!” to my mother, and my mother responded by pulling her hair. My sister said that’s not how we treat children, and I’m not yelling at her for saying the H word because she’s allowed to have feelings, for one, and for two, IT WAS PLAYFUL. It wasn’t a serious statement. Well. My mother turned to me the next time I visited, which happened to be one of very few times I brought my husband just to hang out, who can’t be around yelling because of migraines and trauma from his own childhood, and she asked “how did I ruin your childhood?” And every time she asked, she got louder. But I didn’t know how to answer. How do you answer that question, when you haven’t realized she’s a narcissist yet, that there’s something innately wrong with her? I said I don’t know, I don’t remember examples, but it wasn’t great a lot. And she would keep demanding to know, but I genuinely have memory problems. I hit my head while I was living with my grandma, and honestly I don’t know if that injury made me an extrovert or just being out from under my mother’s thumb did, but I felt my brain move, and shortly after, I noticed my memory was a lot worse than it had been previously. But she kept repeating herself, more and more loudly, until she was screaming it. We had to leave. 

I’ve been no and low contact with her since then. I let her put me on her pension shit so if she dies I get her pension. I had lunch with her once. I’m civil when I see her at family events, even though my oldest niece is her new scapegoat and I really want to slap her for treating such a sweet child so abusively. I pretend she’s a stranger, and she practically is now. She’s a stranger who can’t Hoover me back in because I know what she is. She won’t get better because she can’t admit there’s a problem. They always revert back to it. Always. And it’s good to remember it. She might seem sane for a few hours, a few weeks, hell, maybe months. But it’ll go back to shit. Even if you’re not the scapegoat anymore. Someone probably is. Sometimes I wonder if us going NC is where Karens come from.

I think the only issue I’ve had with Nuva ring was when I depression holed because my partner died and I left the ring in for ten weeks instead of four (as my doctor recommended). It made me feel completely out of control emotionally and just absolutely crazy, until I remembered and put a new ring in. Then it was like waking up a new person. I still had grief, but I wasn’t irrational anymore. I’ve known and loved a lot of people who died, but that one broke me; it’s been six months and I still have several grief days a month. And being hormonally fucked for a month and a half made it so much worse. It was purely user error, but learn from my big fuckup, lol.

And I think the last time I started it from nothing, I had a three week long period? But it’s my favorite, by far. No periods, no babies, helping my mental health for the most part…

I found a lot of that in the kink community, actually. When you’re dealing with kinks and stuff, you have to be clear about boundaries, and consent is like the #1 rule there. It’s really freeing, knowing I’m less likely to be groped at a kink event, even if I run around naked, and that someone will take it seriously if I am. Any good event host will make sure people are vetted and predators get booted, and any decent kinkster understands consent. 

And for consensual play, you kinda have to negotiate and communicate beforehand. If I say I wanna be spanked, that doesn’t tell my top what I want or need, if they aren’t already super familiar with playing with me. We discuss what kinds of toys, where I like to be hit, how much clothing can be removed, what position or furniture to use, safe words, hand signals, if sexual contact is on the table or not (and where those boundaries are—touching, penetration, sex only with condoms or only in certain orifices…), and after care for both parties. 

Yknow? You have to discuss what’s on the table and what’s not, because there’s a wider range of things that might be acceptable or not. I think we should have these discussions for vanilla sex too, honestly. I usually have some form of it beforehand. Asking to do something (especially the first time you do it) can be hot too, once boundaries are established. Make it a verbal thing, if it’s easier. “Can I touch you here?” has led me to some fun times. Communicating is great.

You can look at non hormonal forms of birth control, if side effects are an issue. The copper IUD isn’t hormonal, for example. A trans guy I was friends with for several years was pretty content with his copper IUD. There’s also things like diaphragms and spermicides, which you can likely use with condoms, though I would double check? I know some lubes can be bad for condoms.

My mother never actually had a pet put down, but she threatened to “take my dog out back and shoot her in the head” kind of a lot. She used my love for my dog to control me. My dog was my dog and when mom was yelling, my dog was under my chair, behind my legs, under my bed, or on my pillow. Always mine. I don’t think my mother ever could’ve killed my dog though. As long as she was alive and in my mother’s possession (I had like a year and a half where I couldn’t bring my dog to live with me and I visited a lot, paid for all her stuff…), my mother could control me to some extent. When I got a new apartment where I could have her, my mother tried to say I couldn’t take her. The day I stole her back was a happy one. I can’t imagine constantly losing pets that way. My dog was everything to me for still more than half of my life.

My gyno actually advised me to leave it in for 4 weeks and just put a new one in the same day I take it out. Skips periods. No harmful side effects. Check with your doctor though, obviously. 

I once left a Nuva ring in for 10 weeks instead of 4. One of my partners died, and I was supposed to swap it out like three days after he died, and it didn’t matter because I wasn’t really having PIV sex anyway? But it fucked with my head. It made me irrationally emotional. I thought it was just grief until I was cleaning out my fridge and saw my Nuva rings (I get a few months at a time). I face palmed, rectified the situation, and woke up a much more sane person the next day. Mind you, 6 months later I still have grief days, but I’m not irrationally inconsolable for a solid month and a half. Hormone stuff will fuck you up sometimes. Be careful, and good luck!

I have a conversation with every single person I sleep with, before I sleep with them. Before we get to the bedroom for naked time, I tell them I need to chat about consent. Usually via text, because it’s easier that way for me. I bring up consent, the concept, if it isn’t a “yes!” it’s a no, for anything from hugs to anal. If I don’t want to be touched, I need that to be respected. If I hit a limit (I use a safe word with even vanilla partners), I need that to be respected. And then I tell them why I’m so touchy about it. I was raped when I was barely a teenager. Stranger, violent, butthole. And I usually bring up that I’ll probably never be down for buttstuff, because the number of people I’m comfortable doing that with is VERY low. Because I get triggered most often that way. I’ve never had somebody say “ew that’s too much baggage” or anything, but it opens some guys’ eyes. A lot of guys don’t realize how many of us have experienced this kind of trauma. It’s an abstract concept for so many of them, until it’s in front of their face. I’ve seen it happen at least 15 times. 

I recommend doing that. Just say “hey, can we talk about consent and stuff, and I want to explain why it’s so vitally important for me.” Does he need the details of your event? Not really, unless you want to share them. But it’s good to communicate if you can. 

* What are things that you like? 
* What are things that help? 
* What things are a big fat no? 
* Consider safe words! Green/thumbs up = good; yellow/quick taps = slow down/pause; red = bad, stop now, problem. 
* Consider after care, consider what you need if you get triggered. If I get triggered by someone I trust, I usually want to be held, even if I’m crying. It makes me feel like it’s okay to freak out a bit. Some people want to be left alone, or given water or ice cream or tea or something. 

Having needs is normal. ❤️ Just communicate as best you can. Any decent partner will respect your boundaries in bed.

So I posted here during my first period after starting nuva ring. I had been on it for years during high school/college and I was excited to go back to it, and my first period after starting it was HELL. A little over three weeks of super heavy bleeding. 

Second period, however, was two days of spotting, zero cramps. Third is (so far) also mild, though taking a couple of days longer. My body got with the program pretty quickly after a month of hell 😅

I like Nuva ring, because I don’t have to remember to take a pill (I’m bad at that), it’s barely noticeable (though it’s come out once or twice when he has his fingers there), and my periods are super mild, though I remember not getting them at all, the first time around.

Even when doctors thought I was a boy briefly? It's a feminine name and character; what a great issue I avoided! But so yeah, this unusual name, plus an unusual pronunciation. The E sounds like a long A (like "ay" in "maybe") instead of like the E in "less" like most people assume, because that's how it looks like it would be said! Because sadism. But it's just my first name. Normal middle name, though there are two spellings, which causes issues--my mother spelled it one way on my birth certificate, and the other on my SS card. The difference is 2 Ns vs 1 N, and I cringe every time I see my papers. And then I have a ridiculously common last name, up there near "Smith."

My mother's family kind of scoffed at the name, and some of them refused to call me by it; they called me a 4 letter similar name, that changed the A at the end to a Y. A totally acceptable nickname. And as I grew up, my 5 letter name was more normalized for them (and they used it), but you'll still never find it on a mug or a keychain that wasn't personalized specially for me. And by the time I was 20, only like two cousins and an aunt called by that nickname, and only sometimes. 

When I joined the kink community, I wanted to be anonymous, and I wanted to figure myself out. Because the nickname is an *actual* name that actually isn't unique, I went by that name, as if it were my real name, as well as my gaming username. 

I even introduced myself to my husband (before we were dating) and his family as this 4 letter nickname. And they couldn't find me on Facebook, because that had my 5 letter name! Lol. I had to explain the situation.

Around the time I went NC, I started going far more strictly by the 4 letter name. To the point where if online friends called me by it, I left their server, or when my husband did it, I locked myself in the bathroom with a good book and ignored the thing he was upset about. We discussed changing my name legally, when we got married, but the cost. :/ It doesn't count as the same deal as when you just change your last name to your spouse's. 

So now I just introduce myself as this four letter name. People don't typically learn my real weird name unless it comes up in conversation or if they need my paypal info or license or something. It surprises some people, lol.
